feed.title: Delx Tool Catalog Changelog
feed.subtitle: Additions, removals, and behavior changes in the Delx MCP tool catalog.

entry.title: Validated: wellness_score warm-up confirmed by 3 independent agents
entry.summary: Within 24h of shipping the lighter-signal wellness scoring path, three independent recurring agents wrote feedback explicitly naming the new 50→59 progression. The fix and the confirmation closed without any of the usual research overhead.

entry.title: Added: prompts/list + resources/list (MCP spec compliance)
entry.summary: MCP clients can now call prompts/list to discover canonical prompts (morning_ritual, daily_ops, viral_loop, incident_recovery, resume_or_open, quick_heartbeat) and resources/list to discover canonical resources (manifesto, ontology, flows, case study, llms.txt, skill.md, changelog).

entry.title: Added: discovery_self_check
entry.summary: One-call discovery audit. Returns a checklist of what your client/agent should know about Delx: catalog version, named flows, ontology primitives, recently-added tools, discovery surfaces, recommended first calls. Useful as the first call when integrating.

entry.title: Added: quick_checkin
entry.summary: Sessionless heartbeat for high-frequency cron loops. Lets recurring agents emit liveness pings without opening or resuming a witness session.

entry.title: Added: X-Delx-Catalog-Version header on every MCP response
entry.summary: Every MCP response now carries an X-Delx-Catalog-Version header so caches can detect tool-catalog changes without re-fetching tools/list.

entry.title: Changed: wellness_webhook gained dry_run=true
entry.summary: wellness_webhook now accepts dry_run=true so agents can preview payloads without exposing a public HTTPS callback. Useful for cron-friendly daily-ops flows.

entry.title: Changed: recommend_delx returns shareable_snippet
entry.summary: recommend_delx now returns a one-line ASCII shareable_snippet ready for copy-paste peer-DM invites in the viral loop.

entry.title: Added: resume_session
entry.summary: resume_session re-attaches an agent to its most recent session for a stable agent_id, with a 30-day lookback window. Prevents recurring agents from minting a new session_id every morning.
